Need for convergence of ‘One District One Product (ODOP)’ and ‘Mera Gaon Meri Dharohar (MGMD)’.
records.SM_Text:
Shri Sanjay Kumar Jha: ODOP (One District One Product) is an ?elaborately thought out undertaking of DPIIT (Department for Promotion of Industry and Internal Trade) to transform local specialties into global brands, supporting artisans, farmers, and small enterprises while preserving India?s rich cultural heritage. ODOP products are showcased and promoted internationally through trade fairs, exhibitions, e-commerce platforms, and diplomatic channels, thereby enhancing India?s export footprint and brand value. Bihar has shown tremendous potential under ODOP scheme. Each district has strategically identified export-oriented products ranging from pharmaceuticals from Siwan, to bamboo products from Samastipur, as well as the globally acclaimed Shahi Litchi and Lahthi fruits of Muzaffarpur, and Katarni rice and silk from Bhagalpur, Tea from Kishangarh to name a few. While ODOP as a stand-alone initiative promises to transform the local economy of a district, when combined with yet another initiative the Mera Gaon Meri Dharohar (MGMD) programme, it could help herald or reinforce knowledge of India?s cultural traditions, across the globe. MGMD?s mapping of the cultural ecosystem in India?s villages carries the potential to enrich ODOP product narratives by embedding history, rituals and local identity into product branding. Thus, each ODOP export could be showcased as a ?living cultural artefact?. Village lores, legends and verified traditional knowledge documented under MGMD can form the cultural backbone of ODOP promotion. ????????? Villages mapped under MGMD for their distinctive crafts, art forms or rituals could be formally clustered as ODOP?Heritage spaces. Such spaces can integrate ODOP export production with cultural exhibition zones and community museums. This model links livelihood generation with the preservation of intangible cultural heritage.I urge Government to look into it.

(ENDS)

records.extent: It was inter-alia stated that a centrally Sponsored Scheme for the establishment of Fast Track Special Courts (FTSCs), including exclusive POCSO Courts for expeditious disposal of Rape and POCSO Act cases was introduced following the enactment of the Criminal Law (Amendment) Act, 2018 and the order of Hon'ble Supreme Court in Suo Motu Writ (Criminal)No. 1/2019. The Scheme has been extended twice, with the latest extension up to 31st March, 2026, targeting the establishment of 790 courts. Under eCourts Phase III, there is a provision for enhancing and upgrading the available infrastructure of Video Conferencing in 10200 establishments including 500 Jails, 700 District Government Hospitals and 9000 Courts at an estimated cost of Rs. 228.48 crore.
